idiom_name: ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline (Use/Run) and System.Reflection.DispatchProxy
implementation_notes: C# normally takes the pattern from the platform: the ASP.NET Core request pipeline is a chain of middleware delegates assembled with Use and Run, where each middleware decides whether to invoke the next delegate and can short-circuit, and the runtime builds the chain for every request; for interface-level interception System.Reflection.DispatchProxy generates a proxy class whose Invoke hook sees every call. What replaces the classic structure: the middleware pipeline and DispatchProxy replace hand-written proxy classes and a hand-built chain - write one class per boundary with a single InvokeAsync(HttpContext, RequestDelegate next) and register it in order; the classic form remains justified when the guarded interface is not HTTP (gRPC interceptors, a custom DispatchProxy over a service interface).
pitfalls: Middleware order is security-relevant and fails silently: authentication must precede authorisation, and a gate added after a terminal Run delegate never executes.
Short-circuiting must set the status code before the body is written; touching headers or the status after the response has started throws.
DispatchProxy intercepts interface members only, so a class-based or sealed service needs a hand-written wrapper or the check is skipped.
